# @vllnt/eslint-config

> Strict, opinionated ESLint flat config for TypeScript projects. Every rule enforces error — no warnings, no compromises.

ESLint v9+ flat config with 8 presets: Base, React, Next.js, Node.js, Convex, Turbo, Boundaries, Playwright, plus a shared `ignores` list. TypeScript-first with `strictTypeChecked` + `stylisticTypeChecked`. Prettier built-in. 7 custom Convex lint rules bundled as `eslint-plugin-convex-rules`.

Version 2 requires ESLint >=9, Prettier >=3, and the TypeScript 6 JavaScript API
(`typescript@npm:@typescript/typescript6@^6.0.2`) for type-aware linting. Use
`@typescript/native@npm:typescript@^7.0.2` alongside it for the TypeScript 7 compiler.
TypeScript 5 is not supported. npm latest is stable 2.0.0 at this audit; canary
builds are moving prereleases. See the README installation command.

## Next.js, Playwright and ignores

The Next.js preset accepts route handler exports (`GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`,
`PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`) by exact name and ignores `.next/`, `out/`, `build/` and
`next-env.d.ts`. `@vllnt/eslint-config/playwright` is an opt-in overlay for
`tests/e2e` specs, setup files and `playwright.config.ts` that relaxes
`functional/no-loop-statements`, `max-lines-per-function` and object-key naming
only. `@vllnt/eslint-config/ignores` is a shared ignores list. See
[README](README.md#playwright) and [Shared ignores](README.md#shared-ignores).

## Diagnostics

The package uses ESLint v9+ flat config and needs no extra dependency for the
built-in Config Inspector. From a consuming project, open the inspector with
`pnpm exec eslint --inspect-config` (it downloads on demand and takes no file
argument; pick files in its UI), profile aggregate rule time
with `TIMING=1 pnpm exec eslint .`, or capture per-file parse and rule timings
with `pnpm exec eslint . --stats --format json-with-metadata --output-file eslint-stats.json`.
The inspector explains the effective config but does not measure performance.
See [Inspecting and profiling ESLint](README.md#inspecting-and-profiling-eslint)
for interpretation and benchmarking practices.
